questions.stem: How can you estimate the total population of a species in a large area using quadrat data?

options.text: Count every individual organism in the entire area
Only count organisms in one quadrat and report that number
Calculate the mean number per quadrat and multiply by the total number of quadrats that would fit in the area
Measure the height of organisms and multiply by the area

questions.explanation: To estimate the total population, calculate the mean number of organisms per quadrat from your sample, then scale up by multiplying by the total number of quadrats that would fit in the entire study area. This gives a reliable estimate without counting every individual.
